items.followUp: Define transpiration and explain how water vapour leaves a leaf through the stomata.

rubric.why: Award for defining transpiration as water loss in vapour form from the aerial parts of a plant.
rubric.how: The answer must identify water vapour as being lost from the plant, usually specifying its aerial parts.

rubric.why: These are the essential events inside the leaf before vapour exits through a stoma.
rubric.description: Formation and movement of water vapour inside the leaf
rubric.how: Award for explaining that water evaporates from mesophyll cell surfaces and water vapour enters the intercellular spaces.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the route of escape and show the relevant leaf structures in the section diagram.
rubric.description: Diagram and escape of water vapour
rubric.how: Award for a labelled leaf section showing mesophyll/air spaces and a stoma with guard cells, and arrows showing vapour diffusing out through the stomatal pore.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
Water evaporates from the moist walls of mesophyll cells into the intercellular spaces of the leaf.
Water vapour diffuses through the air spaces and out through the stomatal pore into the atmosphere.
Section diagram: draw and label upper epidermis, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, intercellular air spaces, lower epidermis, guard cells and stomatal pore.
Draw arrows from mesophyll cell surfaces into the air spaces and then out through the stomatal pore.

items.followUp: Define biology and describe one way in which it is useful to humans.

rubric.why: A definition should convey that science is an organized, systematic study of the natural world.
rubric.how: Award full marks for describing science as systematic study or organized knowledge about nature and its laws.

modelAnswer: Science is the systematic study of the natural world and its laws.

items.followUp: Name one important book written by Bu Ali Sina and state the field it concerns.

rubric.why: Bu Ali Sina is chiefly recognised in this context for his work as a physician and medical scholar.
rubric.description: Recognition as a physician or medical scholar
rubric.how: Award for identifying him as a physician, or linking him with medicine.

rubric.why: His famous medical work is a key fact commonly associated with Bu Ali Sina.
rubric.how: Award for naming Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb (The Canon of Medicine), or identifying him as Ibn Sina.

modelAnswer: Bu Ali Sina, also known as Ibn Sina, was a famous Muslim physician and medical scholar.
His well-known medical book is Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb (The Canon of Medicine).

items.followUp: What is meant by the ecosystem level of biological organization?

rubric.why: The biosphere is the highest level of biological organization and includes life and its environments on Earth.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it includes all ecosystems on Earth, or the part/zone of Earth in which life exists.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the highest level of biological organization.
It includes all ecosystems on Earth, where living organisms interact with one another and with their environment.

items.followUp: What structures connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells?

rubric.why: Plasmodesmata are the connecting channels that allow continuity between neighbouring plant-cell cytoplasms.
rubric.how: Award for identifying them as channels or connections through cell walls linking the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells.

modelAnswer: Plasmodesmata are fine channels through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells.
They connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.

items.followUp: State how active transport differs from passive transport in energy use and direction of movement.

rubric.why: Active transport requires energy to move substances against their concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for stating that active transport uses energy and moves substances against the concentration gradient.

rubric.why: Passive transport does not require cellular energy and occurs down the concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for stating that passive transport does not use energy and moves substances down the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Active transport uses energy to move substances against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration.
Passive transport does not use energy; substances move down their concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration.

items.followUp: Define taxonomy and explain what systematics studies.

rubric.why: Taxonomy concerns the identification, naming and classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award for defining taxonomy as the branch of biology concerned with identifying, naming and classifying organisms.

rubric.why: Systematics considers organismal diversity and the relationships among organisms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that systematics studies the diversity of organisms and their relationships.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy is the branch of biology concerned with the identification, naming and classification of organisms.
Systematics is the study of the diversity of organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: Write the taxonomic classification of the mustard plant from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: These entries identify the plant kingdom and the broad plant groups used in its classification.
rubric.how: Award for correctly listing Plantae and the appropriate division and class (accepting standard textbook synonyms).

rubric.why: The order/family/genus/species entries complete the pea plant's classification; standard family and order synonyms are accepted.
rubric.how: Award for correctly listing the order, family, genus Pisum and species sativum, accepting Leguminosae for Fabaceae and the textbook order synonym.

modelAnswer: Kingdom: Plantae
Division: Magnoliophyta (Angiospermae)
Class: Magnoliopsida (Dicotyledonae)
Order: Fabales
Family: Fabaceae (Leguminosae)
Genus: Pisum
Species: sativum (Pisum sativum)
